200.description:
The publisher's own delta: Guide documents released in a date window (`daterange` on the index release date), default segment `notices` (Notices of Change to a NOFO, Notices of Intent to Publish, policy notices, RFIs). `referenced_docnums` on each record names the NOFO a change notice amends (from its title and related documents). Optional `notice_subject` filter. Pages of up to 1000 in rowid order; the cursor pins the window total and fails with `publication_changed` when it moves. When the gateway is unavailable and the segment is `notices`, the official RSS feed is filtered to the window and returned as a partial result.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

200.description:
One Guide document by its number (`docnum`, e.g. PAR-27-053): the index record plus the grants.nih.gov HTML parsed into assistance listing numbers, eligible organizations, number of applications (with the derived `limited_submission`), letter of intent due date, application due dates and expiration date (NOFO pages) or release/effective dates, related announcements, issuer and purpose (notice pages). `document_status` says what happened: `parsed`; `grants_gov_only` when the index has no HTML filename (the NOFO lives only on Grants.gov: use `grants_gov_id` with the grants-gov program); `missing` when grants.nih.gov answered 404 for the listed file; `unrecognized_layout` when the page has none of the Guide labels (legacy documents).

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | object |  |
| `document_status` | string |  |
| `record` | object | One NIH Guide document (NOFO, NOSI or notice) shaped from the Guide search index `_source`. Raw date strings are kept beside parsed dates; free-text deadlines are never converted. Fields the index leaves null stay null; the RSS fallback fills only identity, title, release date and URLs. |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |

document.number_of_applications_text: Applicant organizations may submit more than one application, provided that each application is scientifically distinct. The NIH will not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time, per NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 2.3.7.4 Submission of Resubmission Application. This means that the NIH will not accept: A new (A0) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of an overlapping new (A0) or resubmission (A1) application. A resubmission (A1) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application. 200.description:
The full current list of one index segment (default `active`: the active NOFOs), sorted by rowid ascending, up to 1000 records per page. The cursor pins the segment, the offset, the total and the highest rowid; every page re-reads total and max rowid and fails with `publication_changed` (failure code invalid_input, issue code `publication_changed` at /cursor) when the segment moved, instead of mixing publications. Segments: active, activenosis, expired, expirednosis, notices (notices: about 17 pages). When the gateway is unavailable and the segment is `notices`, the official RSS feed (`/grants/guide/newsfeed/fundingopps.xml`, the latest notices only) is returned as a partial page instead.

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
Cheap version check of the Guide index: per segment (active, activenosis, expired, expirednosis, notices) the record count, the highest rowid and the latest document, plus the newest release date overall. `version` is the SHA-256 of the canonical segment tuples; for segments that fit one page (at most 1000 records) `content_hash` is the SHA-256 of the sorted (rowid, docnum, reldate, expdate) tuples of every record. The index is an API, not a file, so there is no size.
